titles.title: Bible Angels Don't All Look the Same. Here's Why.
titles.reason: Clear correction of a common visual assumption; matches the source comparisons without promising a universal angel catalogue.

titles.title: Six Wings, Four Faces: What the Bible Actually Describes
titles.reason: Specific visual contrast, supported only when tied to the separate Isaiah and Ezekiel passages.

titles.title: Why Biblical Angels Look So Different
titles.reason: Short explanatory promise; narration must distinguish messengers and visionary beings.

titles.title: Would You Recognize an Angel in a Bible Story?
titles.reason: Direct curiosity grounded in hospitality narratives; no real-world encounter prediction.

titles.title: The Angels Behind the Familiar Wings and Halo
titles.reason: Familiar visual premise, but avoid unsupported claims about the history of halos unless additional scholarly evidence is retrieved.

thumbnailConcepts.art: Original Eli surprised beside a clearly labelled-by-Remotion contrast of an ordinary narrative visitor and a six-winged visionary figure; purposeful empty space and one primary focal surprise.
thumbnailConcepts.risk: Do not imply these passages describe the same being.

thumbnailConcepts.art: Original Eli pointing at an original simple illustrated seraphic vision with the exact source-described wing count and paired positions; saturated dark blue separation.
thumbnailConcepts.risk: A visionary interpretation of Isaiah, not the universal appearance of angels.

thumbnailConcepts.art: Original Eli as curious reader, scripture scroll and a clearly separated illustrative eye-covered wheel detail; clean high-contrast composition.
thumbnailConcepts.risk: Eyes on wheel rims in Ezekiel 1; do not falsely attach that detail to every angel.

shortsBoundaryPolicy: Select self-contained original narration from actual ASR word timestamps after synthesis. No fabricated timestamps or mid-sentence crop. Adapt portrait visuals and captions; verify each export before upload.
publishing: Owner authorized an original next video and its scheduling. Upload private only after all QA, then use the existing daily publication slot. Social posting requires connected accounts and a compatible approved publisher.
costPolicy: Existing Cloudflare total cap of 8 USD/month applies; every other provider remains free-only. No new paid service authorized.
blocker: Actions still rejects artifact uploads despite prior cleanup; billing API is inaccessible to this integration. Preflight will stop before any inference if storage is unavailable.
